notes.front: What does `kubeadm upgrade plan` do?
notes.back: Checks that the cluster can be upgraded and fetches the versions you can upgrade to.
notes.explanation: You run it on the first control plane node, after upgrading the kubeadm package, to choose a target version.
notes.example: Like a mechanic's inspection that says "this car can take these parts" before any part is fitted.
notes.evidence: Verify the upgrade plan: sudo kubeadm upgrade plan This command checks that your cluster can be upgraded, and fetches the versions you can upgrade to.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Call kubeadm upgrade"

notes.front: What is `kubeadm upgrade apply`?
notes.back: The command, run on the first control plane node with a target version (`kubeadm upgrade apply v<version>`), that upgrades the control plane.
notes.explanation: It checks the cluster is upgradeable, enforces the version skew policies and upgrades the control plane components, rolling back if any fails to come up.
notes.example: Like the head chef switching the kitchen to a new menu first, before the waiting staff are retrained.
notes.evidence: Upgrades the control plane components or rollbacks if any of them fails to come up.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "How it works"

notes.front: What is `kubeadm upgrade node`?
notes.back: The upgrade command for every node after the first control plane node: other control plane nodes and worker nodes.
notes.explanation: On a worker node it fetches the kubeadm ClusterConfiguration and upgrades the kubelet configuration for that node.
notes.example: Like each branch office installing the update head office has already rolled out.
notes.evidence: kubeadm upgrade node does the following on worker nodes: Fetches the kubeadm ClusterConfiguration from the cluster. Upgrades the kubelet configuration for this node.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "How it works"

notes.front: Is skipping a minor version supported when upgrading a kubeadm cluster?
notes.back: No. Skipping minor versions when upgrading is unsupported.
notes.explanation: Each upgrade goes one minor version at a time, as the Version Skew Policy requires.
notes.evidence: Skipping MINOR versions when upgrading is unsupported. For more details, please visit Version Skew Policy.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters"

notes.front: In a cluster with a single kube-apiserver instance, may the API server skip a minor version when upgraded?
notes.back: No. It must not skip minor versions, even in single-instance clusters.
notes.explanation: The rule comes from the project's policies for API deprecation and API change guidelines.
notes.evidence: Project policies for API deprecation and API change guidelines require kube-apiserver to not skip minor versions when upgrading, even in single-instance clusters.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "Supported component upgrade order"

notes.front: In a highly available cluster, what must be upgraded before kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler and cloud-controller-manager?
notes.back: All kube-apiserver instances.
notes.explanation: The supported upgrade order starts with kube-apiserver, then these control plane components, then kubelet and kube-proxy.
notes.evidence: all kube-apiserver instances must be upgraded before upgrading these components
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "Supported component upgrade order"

notes.front: What must be true before you upgrade a kubelet to the new minor version?
notes.back: The kube-apiserver instances it talks to must already be on that version.
notes.explanation: A kubelet must never be newer than kube-apiserver, so the API server always goes first.
notes.evidence: The kube-apiserver instances the kubelet communicates with are at 1.37 Optionally upgrade kubelet instances to 1.37
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "Supported component upgrade order"

notes.front: Can a kubelet be upgraded by a minor version in place, with its Pods still running?
notes.back: No. In-place minor kubelet upgrades are not supported: drain the node's Pods first.
notes.explanation: Draining moves the node's Pods elsewhere first, so none is running while the kubelet changes minor version.
notes.evidence: Before performing a minor version kubelet upgrade, drain pods from that node. In-place minor version kubelet upgrades are not supported.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "Supported component upgrade order"

notes.front: Before upgrading anything, what three cluster conditions does `kubeadm upgrade apply` check?
notes.back: The API server is reachable; all nodes are Ready; the control plane is healthy.
notes.explanation: These checks confirm the cluster is in an upgradeable state before any component changes.
notes.evidence: Checks that your cluster is in an upgradeable state:The API server is reachable All nodes are in the Ready state The control plane is healthy
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "How it works"

notes.front: On the second and later control plane nodes, how does the upgrade differ from the first?
notes.back: Run `kubeadm upgrade node` instead of `kubeadm upgrade apply`; `kubeadm upgrade plan` and the CNI plugin upgrade are no longer needed.
notes.explanation: On those nodes, `kubeadm upgrade node` upgrades the control plane static Pod manifests and the kubelet configuration.
notes.evidence: Same as the first control plane node but use: sudo kubeadm upgrade node instead of: sudo kubeadm upgrade apply Also calling kubeadm upgrade plan and upgrading the CNI provider plugin is no longer needed.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Call kubeadm upgrade"

notes.front: On an additional control plane node, what does `kubeadm upgrade node` upgrade, besides the kubelet configuration?
notes.back: The static Pod manifests for the control plane components.
notes.explanation: It first fetches the kubeadm ClusterConfiguration and may back up the kube-apiserver certificate.
notes.evidence: kubeadm upgrade node does the following on additional control plane nodes: Fetches the kubeadm ClusterConfiguration from the cluster. Optionally backups the kube-apiserver certificate. Upgrades the static Pod manifests for the control plane components. Upgrades the kubelet configuration for this node.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "How it works"

notes.front: How many control plane nodes should you upgrade at once?
notes.back: One at a time.
notes.explanation: Since v1.28, kubeadm waits until all control plane instances are upgraded before upgrading the addons, so they must be done in sequence.
notes.evidence: The upgrade procedure on control plane nodes should be executed one node at a time.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Upgrading control plane nodes"

notes.front: Which command prepares a node for its kubelet upgrade, marking it unschedulable and evicting its workloads?
notes.back: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets`
notes.explanation: A drain is needed before a minor kubelet upgrade, since in-place minor kubelet upgrades are not supported.
notes.evidence: Prepare the node for maintenance by marking it unschedulable and evicting the workloads: # replace <node-to-drain> with the name of your node you are draining kubectl drain <node-to-drain> --ignore-daemonsets
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Drain the node"

notes.front: After upgrading the kubelet and kubectl packages on a node, which two commands restart the kubelet?
notes.back: `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`, then `sudo systemctl restart kubelet`.
notes.explanation: The documentation restarts the kubelet straight after installing the new packages, before uncordoning the node.
notes.evidence: Restart the kubelet: sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl restart kubelet
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Upgrade kubelet and kubectl"

notes.front: After the kubelet restarts on the upgraded node, which command brings the node back online?
notes.back: `kubectl uncordon <node>`, which marks it schedulable again.
notes.explanation: Draining left the node unschedulable, so it takes no new Pods until uncordoned.
notes.evidence: Uncordon the node Bring the node back online by marking it schedulable: # replace <node-to-uncordon> with the name of your node kubectl uncordon <node-to-uncordon>
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Uncordon the node"

notes.front: How should worker nodes be upgraded?
notes.back: One or a few nodes at a time, without dropping below the minimum capacity your workloads need.
notes.explanation: The documentation ties how many nodes you take at once to keeping enough capacity for your workloads.
notes.evidence: The upgrade procedure on worker nodes should be executed one node at a time or few nodes at a time, without compromising the minimum required capacity for running your workloads.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Upgrade worker nodes"

notes.front: Using the community package repositories (`pkgs.k8s.io`), why might the target version not appear when you upgrade?
notes.back: The repository is per minor release: you must enable the repository for the new minor version.
notes.explanation: The documentation says to check the package repositories if the expected version is missing.
notes.evidence: If you're using the community-owned package repositories (pkgs.k8s.io), you need to enable the package repository for the desired Kubernetes minor release.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Changing the package repository"

notes.front: How many minor versions older than kube-apiserver may a kubelet be, and may it be newer?
notes.back: Up to three minor versions older (two for kubelet older than 1.25); never newer.
notes.explanation: For kubelets older than 1.25 the limit was two minor versions.
notes.evidence: kubelet must not be newer than kube-apiserver. kubelet may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver (kubelet < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older than kube-apiserver).
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "kubelet"

notes.front: In a highly available cluster, how far apart may the newest and oldest kube-apiserver instances be?
notes.back: Within one minor version.
notes.explanation: Skew between API servers also narrows which kubelet versions are supported.
notes.evidence: the newest and oldest kube-apiserver instances must be within one minor version.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "kube-apiserver"

notes.front: For how many recent minor releases does the Kubernetes project maintain release branches?
notes.back: The three most recent minor releases.
notes.explanation: Applicable fixes, including security fixes, may be backported to those three branches.
notes.evidence: The Kubernetes project maintains release branches for the most recent three minor releases
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "Supported versions"

notes.front: A kubeadm cluster runs 1.32 and must reach 1.34. What is the supported path?
notes.choices:
A) `kubeadm upgrade apply v1.34.x` straight away
B) Upgrade to 1.33 first, then from 1.33 to 1.34
C) Upgrade the kubelets to 1.34 first, then the control plane
D) Reinstall the cluster at 1.34
notes.back: B) Upgrade to 1.33 first, then to 1.34: one minor version at a time.
notes.explanation: Skipping minor versions when upgrading is unsupported.
notes.choicesExplained: A skips 1.33. C makes kubelets newer than kube-apiserver, which is never allowed. D is not an upgrade path.
notes.evidence: Skipping MINOR versions when upgrading is unsupported.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters"

notes.front: The control plane is upgraded. Which order is right for worker `node-2`, after upgrading its kubeadm package?
notes.choices:
A) `kubeadm upgrade node`, drain, upgrade kubelet and kubectl, restart kubelet, uncordon
B) Drain, upgrade kubelet, uncordon, then `kubeadm upgrade apply`
C) Upgrade kubelet, restart it, then drain
D) Uncordon, `kubeadm upgrade plan`, restart kubelet
notes.back: A) `kubeadm upgrade node`, drain, upgrade the kubelet and kubectl packages, restart the kubelet, uncordon.
notes.explanation: The drain must come before the kubelet upgrade, because in-place minor kubelet upgrades are not supported, and the node is made schedulable again only at the end.
notes.choicesExplained: B uses `apply`, which is for the first control plane node. C upgrades the kubelet in place before draining. D uncordons first and runs `plan`, which is not needed on workers.
notes.evidence: Before performing a minor version kubelet upgrade, drain pods from that node. In-place minor version kubelet upgrades are not supported.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "Supported component upgrade order"

notes.front: The API server runs 1.35. Which kubelet version is outside the supported skew?
notes.back: D) 1.36: a kubelet must never be newer than kube-apiserver.
notes.explanation: Kubelets may be up to three minor versions older (1.32 to 1.35 here), but never newer.
notes.choicesExplained: A is the same version. B is two minors older. C is three minors older, the limit.
notes.evidence: kubelet must not be newer than kube-apiserver. kubelet may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "kubelet"

notes.front: You have upgraded the kubeadm package on the first control plane node and want to see which versions you can move to. What do you run?
notes.choices:
A) `sudo kubeadm upgrade plan`
B) `sudo kubeadm upgrade node`
C) `kubectl version`
D) `sudo kubeadm upgrade apply --force`
notes.back: A) `sudo kubeadm upgrade plan`
notes.explanation: It checks the cluster can be upgraded and fetches the available versions, before you choose one for `kubeadm upgrade apply`.
notes.choicesExplained: B is for later nodes. C shows current versions only. D forces an apply, used to recover from a bad state, not to plan.
notes.evidence: This command checks that your cluster can be upgraded, and fetches the versions you can upgrade to.
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Call kubeadm upgrade"

notes.front: The newest Kubernetes minor release is 1.37. Which cluster runs a minor version that no longer has a maintained release branch?
notes.choices:
A) A cluster on 1.37
B) A cluster on 1.36
C) A cluster on 1.35
D) A cluster on 1.34
notes.back: D) 1.34: only the three most recent minors (1.37, 1.36, 1.35) have release branches.
notes.explanation: Applicable fixes, including security fixes, may be backported to those three branches only.
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C are the three most recent minor releases, all still maintained.
notes.evidence: The Kubernetes project maintains release branches for the most recent three minor releases (1.37, 1.36, 1.35).
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Version Skew Policy", "Supported versions"

notes.front: `kubeadm upgrade apply` versus `kubeadm upgrade node`: where is each run?
notes.back: `apply`: once, on the first control plane node. `node`: on every other control plane node and on worker nodes.
notes.explanation: Later nodes use `node` instead of `apply`, and no longer need `plan`.
notes.evidence: Same as the first control plane node but use: sudo kubeadm upgrade node instead of: sudo kubeadm upgrade apply
notes.source: Kubernetes documentation, "Upgrading kubeadm clusters", "Call kubeadm upgrade"
